Rashi on Ketubot 56b:10:1.english: [He] said, "One may not make [it]" - And devaluation is also included in the betterment of the world.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:10:2.hebrew: שלא קבל עליו אחריות - הבעל, אם יאבדו. ופריש ליה תנא דלא חייש לזולא אלא לאונסא, וקאמר ליה רבי יוסי: וכי קביל עליו אחריות נמי, מה נתקן העולם בכך? והלא אף כשהן קיימין, אין קצובין ופוחתין:
Rashi on Ketubot 56b:10:2.english: He did not accept responsibility upon himself - [That is,] the husband, if they are lost. And [the Gemara] explains the Tanna [as meaning] that he is not concerned about depreciation, only about unavoidable loss, and Rabbi Yosei says to him: Even when he accepted responsibility upon himself, how is the situation remedied by this? Behold, even while they remain intact, they are not fixed [in value] and they depreciate.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:1:1.english: And we maintain - in [the chapter] HaKotev.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:1:2.english: What [does] “writes” [mean]? “Says” - Thus, his stipulation is a [valid] stipulation.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:3:1.hebrew: והרי חמרים - גבי דמאי, דרבנן הוא, ולא עבדו בהו חיזוק למיחש לגומלין לרבי יהודה:
Rashi on Ketubot 56b:3:1.english: And behold, donkey drivers - Regarding demai, which is rabbinic, and [yet] they did not make a reinforcement for them to be concerned about mutual favoritism, according to Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:4:1.hebrew: שלי חדש - והישן טוב ממנו, שהחדש עדיין אינו יבש כל צרכו, והכי נמי אמרינן באיזהו נשך (ב"מ עב:): היו חדשות מארבע וישנות משלש כו'. ויש מפרשים משום עומר, ולאו מילתא היא; דא"כ דמתרץ בדמאי הקילו, התינח דמאי, חדש מאי איכא למימר? ועוד, לא מצינו שנחשדו עמי הארץ על איסור חדש. ולא נקט לה אלא משום אין נאמנים דדמאי, ורבותא אשמועינן דאע"ג דמשבח לה לדחבריה נמי במילי אחרנייתא, אינו נאמן על הדמאי, דחיישינן לגומלין:
Rashi on Ketubot 56b:4:1.english: Mine is new - and the old [produce] is better than it, because the new [produce] is not yet completely dry. And so too we say in [the chapter] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 72b): "New ones were [sold] at four and old ones at three, etc." Some explain [that "new" refers to the prohibition of new grain before] the omer [offering], but that is not the case; for if so, when [the Gemara] answers that they were lenient regarding demai, that works well for demai, [but] what is there to say regarding chadash [the biblical prohibition of new grain]? Furthermore, we have not found that amei ha'aretz are suspected of [violating] the prohibition of chadash. Rather, [the Mishna] only mentioned it because of [the ruling] "they are not believed" regarding demai, and it teaches us a novelty: that even though he praises his fellow's [produce] in other matters as well, he is [still] not believed regarding demai, because we are concerned about reciprocity [i.e., collusion].

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:5:1.hebrew: בדמאי הקילו - משאר ספק דדבריהם, ואפילו ספק ליתיה, דרוב עמי הארץ מעשרין הן:
Rashi on Ketubot 56b:5:1.english: They were lenient about demai - More than [with] other cases of uncertainty of rabbinic [law], and it is not even an uncertainty, for most amei ha'aretz tithe [their produce].

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:6:1.hebrew: כל הפוחת אפילו בתנאה - מדלא תנא "כל בתולה שאין לה מאתים ואלמנה שאין לה מנה הרי זו בעילת זנות", ש"מ דהכי אשמועינן, שאע"פ שהיא גובה לבסוף דאין תנאו קיים, אפילו הכי, כיון דמעיקרא אתני, קרי לה בעילת זנות, משום דמשעת ביאה לא הוה סמכא דעתה אכתובה:
Rashi on Ketubot 56b:6:1.english: Anyone who reduces [it], even with a stipulation - From [the fact] that [the Mishnah] did not teach, "Any virgin who does not have two hundred [dinars] or widow who does not have a maneh [one hundred dinars], this is licentious intercourse," learn from this that this is what it teaches us: that even though she collects [the full amount] in the end, as his stipulation does not stand, even so, since he stipulated from the outset, it calls [the marriage] licentious intercourse, because from the time of intercourse she did not rely upon [her] marriage contract.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:6:2.english: Apparently he holds [that] his stipulation is void - For otherwise, there is no novelty in [its] stating "anyone who reduces."

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:7:1.english: But haven't we heard him - Earlier.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:8:1.hebrew: ר' יוסי אומר רשאי - ואפילו על פה נמי תנאו קיים. ואתא ר' יהודה למימר נמי רשאי כר' יוסי; מיהו על פה תנאו בטל, כדאמרינן לעיל: חכמים עשו חיזוק לדבריהם יותר משל תורה, אבל באת למחול, תכתוב שובר:
Rashi on Ketubot 56b:8:1.english: Rabbi Yosei says: One is permitted - Even verbally, his stipulation is valid. And Rabbi Yehuda comes to say [that] one is also permitted, like Rabbi Yosei; however, verbally, his stipulation is void, as we said above: The Sages reinforced their words more than [those of] the Torah. Rather, [if] she comes to waive [it], she must write a receipt.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:9:1.english: One does not make a marriage contract [from] movable property - One does not designate movable property for a marriage contract.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:9:2.english: For the betterment of the world - Lest they be lost or their value decrease.

Rashi on Ketubot 56b:9:3.hebrew: אין קצובין - אין דמיהן קצובין עולמית, דמוקרי ומוזלי. הלכך, פעמים שפוחתין מכדי מה ששמאום:
Rashi on Ketubot 56b:9:3.english: [They] are not fixed - Their value is not permanently fixed, for they become expensive and cheap. Therefore, sometimes they depreciate below what they were appraised at.

Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:10:1.hebrew: אבל קבל עליו אחריות עושין - וליכא למיחש שמא יאמר לה "טלי כתובתיך וצאי", כדאמרינן בסוף האשה שנפלו (לקמן כתובות דף פב: ושם); דדוקא בדלא קיבל עליו אחריות איכא למיחש להכי, הואיל ואינו יכול ליהנות מן המטלטלין לעשות בהן סחורה ולהשתכר בהן, שהאשה לא תתן לו הואיל ואין אחריות עליו. אבל היכא דכתב לה "כל נכסי אחראין וערבאין", יכול לייחד ואין לחוש שיאמר לה "טלי כתובתיך וצאי", כיון שיכול ליהנות מהן, שלא תקפיד האשה אם יעשה בהן שום סחורה. והיינו טעמא דאמר בפרק נערה (לעיל כתובות דף נא.) [דתנן: כתב שוה מנה תחת מאתים זוז ולא כתב לה "נכסים דאית לי אחראין", משמע] שיכול לייחד שדה לכתובתה בלא שום אחריות, דכיון שיש לו הנאת אכילת פירות, ודאי לא יאמר לה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:10:1.english: But [if] he accepted responsibility upon himself, they may do so - And there is no concern lest he say to her, "Take your ketubah and leave," as we say at the end of [the chapter] HaIshah SheNaflu (later, Ketubot 82b, and there); for specifically where he did not accept responsibility upon himself is there a concern for this, since he cannot benefit from the movable property to conduct business with it and profit from it, as the wife will not allow him [to do so] since there is no responsibility upon him. But where he wrote to her, "All my properties are responsible and guarantors," he may designate [movable property], and there is no need to be concerned that he will say to her, "Take your ketubah and leave," since he can benefit from it, as the wife will not object if he conducts some business with it. And this is the reason for what it says in the chapter Na'arah (above, Ketubot 51a) [for we learned in a Mishnah: If he wrote "worth a maneh in place of two hundred zuz" and did not write for her "properties that I possess are responsible," it implies] that he may designate a field for her ketubah without any responsibility, for since he has the benefit of consuming [its] produce, he will certainly not say [this] to her.

Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:6:1.english: Anyone who reduces, even with a stipulation - I explained [this] above (Ketubot 51a).

Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:7:1.hebrew: ושמעינן ליה לרבי מאיר דאמר מתנה על מה שכתוב בתורה תנאו בטל הא בדרבנן תנאו קיים - פירש בקונטרס דשמעינן ליה בברייתא דלעיל. וא"ת: מנא ליה למידק "הא בדרבנן תנאו קיים"? דלמא כל שכן דבדרבנן, דעבוד חיזוק טפי, ותנאו בטל כמו לרבי יהודה? וי"ל דדייק מדלא קתני לעיל "על מנת שאין לך עלי שאר, כסות, ועונה, וכתובה"; כיון דאיכא מ"ד דלא עשו חכמים חיזוק לדבריהם אפילו בשל תורה, אע"ג דרבי יהודה מודה בכתובה, מ"מ הוה ליה לשנות, כי היכי דקתני "עונה" אע"ג דמודה בה רבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:7:1.english: And we have heard that Rabbi Meir said: [Anyone who] stipulates counter to that which is written in the Torah, his stipulation is void; thus, in a rabbinic [matter], his stipulation stands - Rashi explained that we heard it from him in the baraita above. And if you ask: From where does [the Gemara] derive to infer "thus, in a rabbinic [matter], his stipulation stands"? Perhaps all the more so in a rabbinic [matter] — where [the Sages] made greater reinforcement — his stipulation is void, just as according to Rabbi Yehuda? And one can answer that [the Gemara] infers [this] from the fact that [the baraita] above does not teach: "On condition that you have no claim against me for food, clothing, conjugal rights, and a marriage contract." Since there is an opinion that the Sages did not reinforce their words even [as in] Torah law, even though Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding the marriage contract, nevertheless [the baraita] should have taught [it], just as it teaches "conjugal rights" even though Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding it:

Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:7:2.hebrew: הא בדרבנן תנאו קיים - תימה, הא שמעינן ליה לרבי מאיר בפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף נה:) דהאוכל תרומת מעשר של דמאי דמוסיף חומש, דעשו חכמים חיזוק לדבריהם כשל תורה; ובריש החולץ (יבמות דף לו: ושם) גבי מעוברת חבירו ומינקת חבירו, שמעינן ליה דעשו חיזוק לדבריהם אף יותר משל תורה! וי"ל, דההיא דיבמות משום דקנסא הוא עשו חיזוק לדבריהם יותר, וההיא דהזהב גבי תרומה — וכן גבי גט דמייתי התם — דאיסורא הוא, התם עשו חיזוק כשל תורה; והכא גבי כתובה, שאינו לא איסור ולא קנס אלא ממונא בעלמא, לא עשו חיזוק כלל:
Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:7:2.english: "Implying that regarding a rabbinic [enactment], his stipulation stands" - [This is] astonishing! For we have heard [regarding] Rabbi Meir in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 55b) that one who eats terumat ma'aser of demai must add a fifth, for the Sages reinforced their words like those of the Torah; and at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 36b, and there [as well]) regarding one who is pregnant by another man or nursing another man's [child], we have heard [from] him that they reinforced their words even more than those of the Torah! And one can answer that in that [case] of Yevamot, because it is a penalty, they reinforced their words more [than those of the Torah]; and in that [case] of HaZahav regarding terumah — and likewise regarding a get (bill of divorce) that is brought there — since it is a prohibition, there they reinforced [their words] like those of the Torah; whereas here regarding a ketubah, which is neither a prohibition nor a penalty, but merely a monetary matter, they did not reinforce [their words] at all.

Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:7:3.hebrew: קסבר רבי מאיר כתובה דאורייתא - אע"ג דכתובת אלמנה דרבנן, מ"מ עיקר כתובה דאורייתא היא. וכעין זה אמרינן בסוף הערל (יבמות דף פא. ושם): אמר ליה רבי יוחנן לר"ל: מי סברת תרומה בזמן הזה דרבנן? א"ל: אין, שאני אומר עיגול בעיגולין עולה. פירוש: ואי תרומה בזמן הזה דאורייתא לא היה עולה, אף על גב דתרומת תאנים דרבנן, כיון דעיקר תרומה מיהא דאורייתא. וא"ת: דתנן לקמן בהכותב (כתובות דף פג: ושם): כתב לה "דין ודברים אין לי בנכסיך בחייך ובמותך כו'", רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר: "ירשנה כו'", ומסיק אליבא דרב דירושת הבעל דרבנן, וחכמים עשו חיזוק לדבריהם כשל תורה — ומה צריך להאי טעמא? אפילו לא עשו חיזוק לדבריהם, תיפוק ליה משום דעיקר ירושה דאורייתא! וי"ל: דלא דמיא ירושת הבעל לשאר ירושות שבאות מחמת קורבה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:7:3.english: Rabbi Meir holds [that] a ketubah is of Torah [origin] - Even though a widow's ketubah is rabbinic, nevertheless the primary ketubah is biblical. And similarly we say at the end of [the chapter] Ha'arel (Yevamot 81a and ibid.): Rabbi Yochanan said to Reish Lakish: "Do you think terumah nowadays is rabbinic?" He said to him: "Yes, for I say a pressed cake of figs [of terumah] is neutralized among [ordinary] pressed cakes of figs." Explanation: If terumah nowadays were biblical, it would not be neutralized — even though terumah of figs is rabbinic — since the essence of terumah, at any rate, is biblical. And if you ask: For we learned in a Mishnah later in [the chapter] HaKotev (Ketubot 83b and ibid.): [If a husband] wrote to her, "I have neither claim nor right to your property, in your lifetime and after your death, etc.," Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: "He inherits her, etc." And [the Gemara] concludes according to Rav that a husband's inheritance is rabbinic, and the Sages reinforced their enactments like those of the Torah — why is this reason necessary? Even if they had not reinforced their enactments, let it be derived from the fact that the essence of inheritance is biblical! And one can answer: A husband's inheritance is not comparable to other inheritances, which come on account of kinship.

Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:9:1.hebrew: אין עושין כתובת אשה מטלטלין - והא דאמרינן בפ"ק (לעיל כתובות דף ז.): "אמר להו אתפסוה מטלטלי" — כשקבל עליו אחריות אם יאבדו או יזולו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 56b:9:1.english: "A woman's marriage contract may not be made [from] movable property" - And [as for] that which we say in the first chapter (above, Ketubot 7a), "he said to them: Assign movable property to her" — [that is] when he accepted responsibility upon himself [for them] if they are lost or depreciate.
